themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration Wave
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights residents filed 22 sidewalk condition complaints (193% above the 7.5-complaint weekly average) and 6 dangling street sign complaints (500% above the 1.0-complaint weekly average), suggesting a coordinated or weather-related infrastructure failure affecting pedestrian safety.
evidence: Sidewalk Condition complaints: 22 filed 2 weeks ago vs. 7.5 weekly average (z-score 9.67)
Street Sign - Dangling complaints: 6 filed last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (z-score 7.07)
Combined spike indicates pattern rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent weather (snow/ice from Jan data) triggered cascading infrastructure failures; check DOT response times
Map the geographic concentration of complaints—are they clustered in specific neighborhoods (Heights vs. Fort Greene) or along major thoroughfares?

themes_detail.label: Construction & Plumbing Surge
themes_detail.summary: This past week, residents filed 33 general construction/plumbing complaints (197% above the 11.1-complaint weekly average, z-score 5.67), the highest spike in the dataset after sidewalk failures, potentially indicating water main breaks, building code violations, or coordinated renovation activity.
evidence: General Construction/Plumbing complaints: 33 filed last week vs. 11.1 weekly average (197% spike, z-score 5.67)
1044 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days, with 759 alteration permits suggesting active renovation citywide
Spike is THIS WEEK, making it most time-sensitive infrastructure concern
reporting_angles: Contact DOB and DEP to determine if water main breaks or sewer overflows are driving the spike; cross-check with utility work orders
Interview residents in neighborhoods with highest complaint density to understand whether renovations are causing dust/noise complaints and whether contractors are licensed

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Abandonment & Disorder Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, derelict vehicle complaints jumped to 12 (465% above the 2.1-complaint weekly average, z-score 5.2) while vehicle noise complaints reached 21 (105% above 10.2 average), and illegal posting surged to 3 complaints (700% above 0.4 average), suggesting a broader public order deterioration in specific blocks.
evidence: Derelict Vehicles: 12 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.1 weekly average (z-score 5.2)
Noise - Vehicle: 21 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 10.2 weekly average (z-score 5.42)
Illegal Posting: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score 5.42)
Graffiti: 10 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.6 weekly average (z-score 4.84)
reporting_angles: Map derelict vehicle locations to identify whether they cluster near transit hubs, parking enforcement gaps, or low-police-visibility blocks
Interview NYPD and sanitation enforcement to understand whether these complaints reflect actual abandonments or enforcement backlog

themes_detail.label: Sanitation & Litter Infrastructure Gap
themes_detail.summary: Three weeks ago, litter basket requests spiked to 14 complaints (647% above the 1.9-complaint weekly average, z-score 6.17), suggesting residents perceive insufficient trash receptacle coverage or maintenance, a long-standing community board budget request around maintenance equipment.
evidence: Litter Basket Request: 14 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.9 weekly average (z-score 6.17)
Community Board has standing request for 'New equipment for maintenance' (Department of Parks and Recreation), suggesting systemic underinvestment
Heat/Hot Water (1663 complaints over 90 days) and Snow/Ice (918 complaints) remain high-volume baseline issues
reporting_angles: Audit Parks Dept. litter basket inventory and maintenance schedule in CD 302; compare to other community districts
Determine whether the 3-week-old spike has sustained or resolved, and whether it correlates with seasonal behavioral change or failed street furniture

themes_detail.label: Heat & Hot Water Crisis Baseline
themes_detail.summary: Heat/Hot water complaints remain the third-highest complaint category at 1663 over 90 days (after illegal parking at 6247 and noise at 1800), but no recent spike data is available; this long-running issue should be monitored for acceleration as winter peaks.
evidence: 1663 Heat/Hot Water complaints over 90 days (third-highest category)
No spike data provided for recent weeks, suggesting sustained baseline rather than new acceleration
Community Board has standing requests for building/housing-related improvements, consistent with heat/water vulnerability
reporting_angles: Request weekly heat complaint breakdowns from 311 to determine if THIS WEEK or LAST WEEK saw a spike; if so, escalate priority
Identify which buildings appear most frequently in heat complaints and investigate ownership, HPD violation history, and tenant demographics
